t: Event Extraction Engine: a plain-language overview
title: Event Extraction Engine: a plain-language overview
description: Overview: what the Event Extraction Engine does and why archives need it. An event extraction engine reads text and answers the reporter's questions: what happened, who was involved, when, where, and what came of it. A sentence like 'In 1969, Apollo 11 landed on the Moon' becomes a structured event with each piece labeled. Narratives become timelines.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Event Extraction Engine works
title: How the Event Extraction Engine works
description: Overview: what the Event Extraction Engine does and why archives need it. Real engines detect event triggers — usually verbs or nominalizations like 'landed', 'election', 'acquisition' — classify the event type against an ontology (ACE, FrameNet frames), then attach arguments in semantic roles: agent, patient, time, location, instrument. Temporal expressions are normalized to dates with tools like SUTime, locations are geocoded, and coreference links 'the mission' back to 'Apollo 11'. Each event frame carries its source sentence and role-level confidence scores.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Event Extraction Engine works: the deep tour
title: How the Event Extraction Engine works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Event Extraction Engine does and why archives need it. Real engines detect event triggers — usually verbs or nominalizations like 'landed', 'election', 'acquisition' — classify the event type against an ontology (ACE, FrameNet frames), then attach arguments in semantic roles: agent, patient, time, location, instrument. Temporal expressions are normalized to dates with tools like SUTime, locations are geocoded, and coreference links 'the mission' back to 'Apollo 11'. Each event frame carries its source sentence and role-level confidence scores. Advanced systems handle event coreference (two sentences describing the same landing merge into one event), subevents and causality between events, and reported-speech attribution ('officials said') so claims are not presented as established fact. Quality is measured by trigger and argument F1 on annotated corpora like ACE 2005. The limits are vague narratives, hypothetical events, and fiction — the engine tags events by modality (actual, hypothetical, negated) and source genre instead of asserting everything it reads.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.
